scope: Qwen3.5-0.8B, local RTX 4060 Laptop SM89, vLLM 0.28.1rc1.dev312+g41848caa6, V1 model runner compatibility path
method: Read-only EngineArgs.create_engine_config construction with the same model, dtype and compatibility environment as the benchmark. No model weights were loaded and no performance claim is derived from this configuration probe.
interpretation: The current benchmark did not leave vLLM's async scheduler disabled: vLLM automatically selected AsyncScheduler and a two-batch in-flight queue even on the V1 model-runner compatibility path.

The original KERNEL-table-only interpretation omitted 186 CUDA Graph replay bodies totaling 542.246 ms and falsely assigned roughly 72% of TPOT outside kernels. The corrected conservative decomposition leaves only 0.243 ms/token (5.71%) outside observed GPU activity; direct interval unions find 3.967 ms GPU-busy and 0.342 ms GPU-idle on average between adjacent within-request graph starts.
A no-async versus async benchmark would measure the value of an already-enabled vLLM feature, not produce a candidate that beats stock vLLM.
The V2 runner remains unavailable in this WSL environment because its UVA precondition failed. That is an environment limitation, not evidence that a V2 runner would achieve a particular speedup.

decision.next_architecture_gate: Only reopen runtime orchestration for a mechanism that changes the dependency chain, such as device-resident multi-token execution or a runner path that is demonstrably available, and require a predicted whole-step gain of at least 3% before implementation.
